headline: V&A Union Suspend Planned Strikes after Management Delivers New Offers
summary: A planned strike across all four Victoria and Albert Museum sites has been suspended as unionized staff return to the negotiating table following a new offer from management. The strike would have affected all four V&A sites: the flagship museum in South Kensington, the Young V&A children’s museum in East London, V&A East, and V&A East Storehouse. The union called a two-day strike in September.

headline: Tate Britain Receives Gift Of 50 Works By Artists Who Lived And Worked In South Asia
summary: British art historian Charles Greig has gifted 50 works from his collection to Tate Britain . Three watercolors combining Indian and European artistic traditions by Sita Ram—included among the donated works—were “ company paintings ,” produced for patrons from the British East India Company. Many of the collection’s paintings highlight the social, political, and cultural changes brought on by British colonialism in South Asia.

headline: “Guaranteed to Sell”: $80 Million Klimt Landscape Heads to Auction
summary: Gustav Klimt ’s 1915–16 Litzlbergkeller is set to hit the auction block in New York next month with an estimate of $60 million to $80 million. Held in a private collection since 1997, Litzlbergkeller set a record for the artist that year when its owner paid $14.7 million (roughly $30.9 million, adjusted for inflation) for it at a Sotheby’s New York auction. Provenance doesn’t sell paintings, however.
